label: H.R. 8883

latest_action.text: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute by the Yeas and Nays: 27 - 16.

selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: H.R. 8883, the Protecting Seniors and Stopping Fraudsters Act, establishes new oversight, screening, survey, and data submission requirements for Medicare hospice programs and home health agencies to combat fraud and monitor program integrity.

affected_groups.effect: Subject to more frequent surveys, mandatory revalidations in certain states, increased penalties for failing to submit quality data, and stricter enrollment screening and fingerprinting for extreme-risk locations.
Subject to increased survey frequencies for new or changed entities, stricter penalties for missing quality data, and enhanced enrollment screening including fingerprinting in high-risk areas.
Will receive mandatory written notices explaining their hospice election, rights, and options within 15 calendar days.

key_provisions: Requires certain established hospice programs in specific states to undergo enrollment revalidation within one year.
Mandates annual surveys for newly enrolled hospice programs and home health agencies, those with ownership changes, or those with reactivated billing privileges during their first 36 months.
Increases payment reductions from 2 percent or 4 percent to 15 percentage points for hospice programs and home health agencies that fail to submit required quality data starting in fiscal year 2029.

Requires stricter screening, including fingerprinting for administrators and medical directors and proof of comprehensive liability insurance, for programs identified as being at extreme risk of fraud.
Establishes annual reporting requirements for the Department of Health and Human Services regarding program integrity, audits, and enforcement actions involving hospices and home health agencies.
Extends adjustments to the calculation of the Medicare hospice cap amount through 2036.
Requires written notice to individuals who elect hospice care within 15 calendar days, detailing program information, rights, and contact resources.
missing_information: Exact state or geographic criteria that define which areas are designated as being at extreme risk of fraud are left to the Secretary of Health and Human Services to determine.
summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 8883, the Protecting Seniors and Stopping Fraudsters Act, establishes new oversight, screening, survey, and data submission requirements for Medicare hospice programs and home health agencies to combat fraud and monitor program integrity.
summary_detail.significance: H.R. 8883 implements substantial changes to Medicare administrative oversight by significantly tightening rules, screening procedures, and penalties for home health agencies and hospice programs, while funding additional federal program integrity activities.
